stem: An example of physical change –
expl: A physical process is a process in which, on removing the cause, the substance involved returns to its original state. A physical process is temporary and reversible. Dissolving sugar in water is a physical change because sugar can be obtained again by evaporation.

stem: Which of the following is not a physical change?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Burning coal is an example of a chemical change, whereas melting of ice and dissolving salt in water are examples of physical changes. A chemical change occurs as a result of a chemical reaction, while a physical change occurs when the form changes but the chemical composition does not change.

stem: According to chemistry, which of the following is an example of a physical change?

options.label: d
options.text: Formation of a green layer on copper utensils

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Boiling of water is a physical change because when heat is removed, the water vapor returns to its original state (water). Other examples—melting of ice, melting of wax, etc.

stem: What is the law in which under the same conditions of temperature and pressure, equal volumes of all gases contain equal number of molecules?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to Avogadro’s law, at the same temperature and pressure, equal volumes of all ideal gases contain the same number of particles or molecules. The number of molecules in one gram-mole of a gas is called the Avogadro number.

stem: What is condensation?

options.label: a
options.text: The change of gas into solid

options.label: b
options.text: The change of solid into liquid

options.label: c
options.text: The change of vapour into liquid

options.label: d
options.text: The change of heat energy into cooling energy

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: When a gas changes into a liquid, this process is called condensation, that is condensation is the process in which vapour (gas) cools down and changes into the liquid state. Examples—clouds, fog, rain, etc.

stem: the amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass of the solution/solvent is known as _____ in Chemistry.
expl: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass is called the concentration of the solution in chemistry. A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more components. A homogeneous mixture means that the composition and properties are uniform throughout. Generally, the component present in larger quantity is called the solvent. The solvent determines the physical state in which the solution exists. Besides the solvent, one or more components present in the solution are called solutes.

expl: The Faraday constant is a universal constant. Its value is approximately 96485 coulombs per mole. The total amount of charge carried by one mole of electrons is defined as the Faraday constant.

stem: For two liquids A and B to form an ideal solution

options.label: a
options.text: Entropy of mixing must be zero

options.label: b
options.text: Free energy of mixing should be zero

options.label: c
options.text: Enthalpy of mixing should be zero

expl: To obtain an ideal liquid (ideal solution) by mixing liquids A and B, the enthalpy of mixing must be zero. In an ideal solution, there is no interaction between molecules. Zero enthalpy means that during mixing, heat is neither absorbed nor released.

stem: The process of separating different dissolved constituents of a mixture by their adsorption on an appropriate material is called :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: The process of separating different liquid components of a mixture by adsorption on a suitable substance is called chromatography. This method is based on the fact that different components of a mixture have different adsorption capacities; therefore, they get adsorbed at different distances on an adsorbent substance and are thus separated.

stem: Process of solid camphor into camphor vapour is called:
expl: The process of converting solid camphor into vapour is defined as sublimation. Some solids, when heated, do not change into the liquid state; instead, they directly change into vapour, and on cooling, the vapour directly changes back into solid. Such substances are called sublimates, and the process is called sublimation. By this method, substances like camphor, naphthalene, ammonium chloride, etc. are purified.

stem: What is the process of a substance changing directly from solid to gas called?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The process of converting solid camphor into vapour is defined as sublimation. Some solids, when heated, do not change into the liquid state; instead, they directly change into vapour, and on cooling, the vapour directly changes back into solid. Such substances are called sublimates, and the process is called sublimation. By this method, substances like camphor, naphthalene, ammonium chloride, etc. are purified.

stem: the Pressure gauge is not given in the domestic LPG cylinders because-

options.label: b
options.text: They cannot represent the quantity of gas in LPG cylinders

expl: In a cylinder containing liquefied gas, the pressure remains constant even when the quantity of gas decreases. Therefore, a pressure gauge cannot indicate the correct amount of gas left in the cylinder.

stem: Which of the following slows down the reaction rate?
expl: In the given options, all are related to catalysts, which affect the rate of a chemical reaction. A catalyst works to increase the rate of a chemical reaction. The rate of any chemical reaction depends on the concentration of reactants, catalyst, temperature, and the nature of reactants. Therefore, the correct option is (d).

stem: Substances that readily absorb moisture from other substances without chemically reacting with them are called

expl: Such substances, which easily absorb moisture from other substances without any chemical reaction, are called desiccants/hygroscopic substances.

stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. Crystallization is the process of deriving crystals of pure substance from their solution.
2. A bonding between constituent atoms or molecules takes place during crystallization.
3. It is an example of chemical change.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: The process of obtaining crystals of pure substances from their solutions is called crystallization. During crystallization, van der Waals forces/interactions are established among the particles. No new chemical substance is formed in the process of crystallization. Hence, it is not a chemical change.

expl: A colloid is a heterogeneous mixture in which very fine particles of one substance remain dispersed in another substance. Common examples include smoke, fog, shaving cream, etc.

stem: What physical process is the release of molecular oxygen from leaves?

options.label: d

expl: The release of molecular oxygen from leaves is an example of diffusion. Diffusion is the process in which two or more substances mix spontaneously to form a homogeneous mixture. expl: Among the options given above, being irreversible, formation of new substances, and absorption of energy are characteristics of a chemical change, whereas “no net change in energy” is involved is not a characteristic of a chemical change.

stem: The process in which atmospheric carbon dioxide is converted into carbohydrates during photosynthesis is -

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In the process of reduction, atmospheric carbon dioxide is converted into carbohydrates during photosynthesis. During photosynthesis, two substrates (CO and HO) react in the presence of light to form two products (carbohydrates and oxygen).

stem: Which of the following pairs will give displacement reactions ?
expl: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from the solution of its salt. Copper (Cu) is more reactive than silver (Ag). Therefore, when copper metal is placed in a silver nitrate (AgNO) solution, copper displaces silver and copper nitrate, [Cu(NO)], is formed. Cu + 2AgNO → Cu(NO) + 2Ag Hence, the reaction between AgNO solution and copper metal is an example of a displacement reaction. Copper (Cu) is less reactive than sodium; therefore, it cannot displace sodium from sodium chloride (NaCl) solution. Copper (Cu) and silver (Ag) are both less reactive than iron (Fe); therefore, they cannot displace iron from iron sulphate (FeSO ) solution. Aluminium (Al) is less reactive than magnesium (Mg); therefore, it cannot displace magnesium from magnesium chloride (MgCl) solution.

stem: The process in which oxidation number decreases is known as :

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: A reaction in which the oxidation number increases is called oxidation, and the one in which the oxidation number decreases is called reduction.

stem: In one of the following options, materials are arranged in increasing order of the force of attraction between their particles. Choose the correct option :
expl: The force acting between the molecules of a substance is called intermolecular force. It is maximum in solids and minimum in gases. In liquids, this force is greater than in gases but less than in solids. Therefore, among the given options, option (a) is the correct answer.

stem: In which of the following medicine production, ethyl alcohol can be used?

expl: Ethyl alcohol or ethanol is used in the production of pharmaceuticals, polymers, leather, polish, plasticizers, cosmetics, etc. It is also used in the production of antiseptic, antipyretic, and anti allergic medicines.

expl: Solids do not have the ability to flow easily. A solid has a definite shape and volume. Solids are mainly of two types— crystalline solids and amorphous solids.

expl: Dilution of sulfuric acid (HSO) and the reaction of water with quicklime are examples of exothermic reactions. A chemical reaction in which heat is released along with the products is defined as an exothermic reaction.

stem: Which of the following represents the suitable condition for the liquefaction of gases ?
expl: For liquefaction of gases, the suitable condition is low temperature and high pressure. This is because, at high pressure and low temperature, gas molecules come closer to each other and their kinetic energy decreases; as a result, gases change into the liquid state.
